summary: WorldEntity duplicate-diagnostic retention is type/exactness bounded but not practically resource bounded: generation-2 PR #293 accepts duplicateDiagnosticCapacity up to 2^53-1, allowing callers to configure an effectively unbounded diagnostics array despite project bounded-cache/queue rules.
evidence: PR #293 exact head c301d8403d3c1b93ee3b2988f80e9d1e689eb33d routes duplicateDiagnosticCapacity through assertNonNegativeInteger, whose upper bound is MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9007199254740991.

createRegistry retains duplicate diagnostics in a Lua array and evicts only once #duplicates >= capacity, so a caller-selected huge capacity removes any meaningful operational memory bound for a long-lived registry.

WorldEntity.DEFAULT_DUPLICATE_DIAGNOSTIC_CAPACITY is 64, demonstrating that this collection is intended to be bounded observability state rather than canonical identity data requiring the full safe-integer domain.
Current generation-2 tests cover false, hostile/metatable-backed, negative/fractional/non-finite capacity handling but do not lock a practical maximum capacity.

Open PR search found no separate WorldEntity duplicateDiagnosticCapacity practical-cap repair; #293 already owns overlapping WorldEntity source/tests, so the follow-up must be sequenced after #293 rather than competing with it.

recommendedAcceptance: introduce an explicit project-owned practical maximum for duplicateDiagnosticCapacity distinct from MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
reject max+1 before any diagnostic-array mutation or comparison loop
lock default, zero, exact maximum, and first-over-maximum behavior with deterministic regressions
document the bounded-retention/performance rationale and preserve duplicate diagnostic FIFO semantics
metadata.suggestedMaximumRationale: 16x the current default of 64 while remaining a small fixed observability buffer; implementer/reviewer may choose another documented small project-owned cap without changing the finding.
